ordered_diagnoses: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris muscle

s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital facial asymmetry with abnormal lip movement
salient_findings: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
key_facts: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
Symmetric frowning, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, and nasolabial fold depth
Normal magnetic resonance imaging of temporal bones and internal auditory canals

shortlist: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris muscle

shortlist.label: Congenital Lower Lip Palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the patient's presentation of right lower lip deviation when smiling or crying

shortlist.label: Asymmetric crying face syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by asymmetric facial movement, consistent with the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Moebius Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Although typically involves more extensive facial weakness, it remains a plausible consideration given the patient's congenital facial asymmetry

shortlist.label: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris muscle
shortlist.why_kept: Specifically involves the muscle responsible for lower lip movement, aligning with the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Hemifacial Microsomia
shortlist.why_kept: A condition that can present with facial asymmetry, although the patient's relatively mild symptoms and normal neurodevelopmental examination make it a less likely but still plausible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The key fact that the right lower lip deviates inward when the child smiles or cries, but the face is symmetric at rest and other facial movements are symmetric, is most consistent with Asymmetric crying face syndrome.

rejected.label: Congenital Lower Lip Palsy
rejected.why: It would likely cause more significant and constant facial asymmetry, not just when smiling or crying.

rejected.label: Moebius Syndrome
rejected.why: It typically involves more extensive facial paralysis and other cranial nerve deficits, not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris muscle
rejected.why: While possible, the specific presentation of asymmetric crying face syndrome is a more precise match for the described symptoms.

rejected.label: Hemifacial Microsomia
rejected.why: It involves underdevelopment of one side of the face, which is not described in the vignette.
